saints.name: St. Guntram
saints.title: King of Burgundy
saints.shortBlurb: A Frankish king of the sixth century remembered for penance, almsgiving, and peacemaking among his warring kin…
biography: Born at Soissons in 532, a son of Chlothar I and grandson of Clovis, Guntram received a fourth of the Frankish realm at his father's death in 561 and ruled the kingdom of Orléans, later called Burgundy, for thirty-one years. Gregory of Tours, who knew him well, habitually calls him 'good king Gontrand'.

His early life was not blameless: he put away wives and lost his sons, two of them to dysentery in 577. Stricken with remorse, he gave himself to fasting, prayer, and almsgiving, open-handed above all in famine and plague, and he forgave even those who tried to take his life.

He built and endowed churches and monasteries, among them the church of St. Marcellus at Chalon-sur-Saône, and by the Treaty of Andelot in 587 secured peace with his nephew and adopted heir, Childebert II. He died at Chalon on 28 March 592 and was buried in his own foundation, his subjects at once acclaiming him a saint.
saints.knownFor: His penance, charity, and peacemaking as a Christian king.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 28 March
